newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico grants first natgas permit in Chihuahua.
newsitem.headline: Mexico grants first natgas permit in Chihuahua.

text.p: Mexico on Wednesday granted the first permit to distribute natural gas in the northern state of Chihuahua to a consortium led by Enova International, a unit of California-based Enova Corp, officials said.
Other members of the consortium are Mexico's private Proxima Gas SA and the U.S.-based Pacific Enterprises International. Pacific Enterprises and Enova plan a $5.2 billion merger.

The consortium, whose commercial name is Ecogas SA, plans to spend $50 million on the project over the next five years and expects to supply natural gas to more than 51,000 users, said a statement by Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission.
The 30-year distribution permit was announced at a seminar on natural gas in Mexico led by Mexican Energy Minister Jesus Reyes Heroles.
Heroles outlined Mexico's natural gas distribution program, which seeks to boost natgas output to 6.2 billion cubic feet per day by the year 2000, the statement said.
